B-VER11R-01 is closed on the artifact side and re-wording is genuinely dead as an attack: the rule never reads the words. I performed both repoints on disk in isolated copies. Declared v23: 8 findings, 2 rounds, 8 leaf edits, reachedExitZero true. Measured v23: 26 findings, 4 rounds, 35 leaf edits, DID NOT REACH EXIT 0. Declared v24: 9 / 2 / 9 / true. Measured v24: 27 findings, 4 rounds, 36 leaf edits, DID NOT REACH EXIT 0. centralClaimAdjudications.adjudication: The relocation is REAL, and it is the right repair. v11's instrument asked what a sentence says; v12's asks whether the artifact may author the position at all, and that question has no wording in it. centralClaimAdjudications.reasoning: notClaimed[2] makes exactly two assertions and both are true: it disclaims class closure, and it asserts that no string leaf is free prose. After parsing there is precisely one `role` string leaf and it is RENDERED, so the duplicate-key plant does not touch it. The v11 reviewer's complaint — that a neighbouring claim was scrupulously scoped while the load-bearing one was not — is inverted here: the disclaimer is exact and the RESIDUAL overreaches. R-VER12-01's 'the surface an editor must move to plant a seal is 2 files rather than 1' and knownLimitations[32]'s 'what v12 closes is the one-file edit' are both claims about EDIT COST, not about leaves, and I falsified both with a one-file edit. This matters more than a wording quibble because R-VER12-01 is the residual the freeze record will carry forward as the standing statement of what v12 left open, and it understates it by the whole file-versus-model gap.
centralClaimAdjudications.isNoFreeProseARealRepairOfTheClassOrHasT: IT IS A REAL REPAIR, and I say that having tried hard to say otherwise. It is not a relabelling: it changes the attack from one that costs a sentence to one that costs a coordinated edit across two files with different owners and different freeze status, and it makes the entire re-wording family — the family that defeated v11 at 28 of 28 — cost nothing to the attacker and gain nothing. My 16974-candidate sweep is the measurement I would want a reader to weigh. BUT THE DEFECT HAS ALSO MOVED, AND NOT ONLY WHERE THE RECORD SAYS. The record says it moved to check-versioning-v12.py, and it did. It ALSO moved to the parse, which the record does not know about and therefore does not publish, and the parse is reachable in one file by an editor with no checker access at all. So: a real repair of the class, with a published relocation that is accurate as far as it goes and incomplete by exactly one layer.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The AST purity measure counts only ast.For, ast.AsyncFor and ast.comprehension, so a while loop, a recursion or a loop-free builder sized from a parameter is invisible to it; registryPurity.theGate overstates what the provenance gate closes.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: Five constructions of mine score 0 on BOTH instruments while being genuine artifact-sized registry builders: a while loop (which reports loopCount 0 as well as parameterSizedLoops 0 — the measure does not see a loop at all), dict.fromkeys over an artifact list, a builder sized from a module global rather than a parameter, a recursive builder, and a map/zip builder. The author's own three constructions score parameterSizedLoops 1 and are correctly caught, so the measure is a real improvement over the name-level lint — it is simply not complete in the direction its gate sentence claims.
nonBlockingObservations.adjudication: Non-blocking because nothing in the closure rests on it and because R-VER12-03 already scopes the measure as conservative and the table as hand-authored. But R-VER12-03 discloses the measure as OVER-tainting, the safe direction, and does not disclose that it UNDER-detects whole loop forms, the unsafe direction; and registryPurity.theGate's 'A future editor who adds a parameter that sizes a loop must declare where its size comes from, or this check fails naming the pair' is false as written. Counting ast.While and ast.Call-shaped iteration, or declaring the measure's node set as a published boundary the way every other boundary here is published, would close the gap between the sentence and the instrument.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The set of functions the purity gate measures is itself a hand-authored constant, and authored() — the function that actually determines the authored registry's key set — is not in it.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: REGISTRY_BUILDERS is the checker constant ('carried_registry','asof_registry','authored_registry'). authored_registry() is a one-line comprehension over m['authored']; the map it consumes is built by authored(), which by this checker's own ast_structural measure has 20 loops and 10 parameter-sized loops on parameter `m`. authored() is never measured, and the pair ('authored','m') never appears in the measured set, so it is never required to appear in PROVENANCE.
nonBlockingObservations.adjudication: Not a defect of these bytes — I traced every loop in authored() and each is sized by a checker constant, by the pinned predecessor's knownLimitations count, by the pinned review's wording count, or by the deps-gated audit, and my reconstruction of the artifact from the instrument is the empirical confirmation. Recorded because the provenance gate is presented as the structural successor to 'it is not possible to write an artifact-sized loop', and a gate whose subject list is hand-maintained inherits one more hand-authored step than R-VER12-03 discloses. Deriving REGISTRY_BUILDERS from the functions whose results actually reach a registry, or simply adding authored() to it, would cost nothing.

nonBlockingObservations.title: claim-register.v1.json is a second surface that renders into the artifact, and the published relocation names only check-versioning-v12.py.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: Rendered leaves take their values from the live unpinned register at registerAsOfAudit.liveD9Binding, .liveVersioningBinding, .liveRetentionTiersBinding and entries[*].registerBinding, and those values are interpolated into knownLimitations[35] and into R-VER12-06's measured text. Appending prose to the VERSIONING binding produced 34 findings including two VER12-RENDER subtree mismatches and a VER12-PRED the artifact cannot clear, because every register binding that reaches a rendered leaf is also read by the pinned predecessor pair. nonBlockingObservations.title: The rehearsal's _DERIVED bundle is measured once at depth 0 and reused by every nested run, which is correct for the sweeps and incorrect for the rehearsals.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: derive() is called once per outer run and its results are read by every inner() call. For append_sweep() and boolean_sweep() this is right and necessary — the measurements are properties of the base subject and re-deriving them inside each candidate would make every candidate red for unrelated reasons and would measure nothing. For rehearse_live() it is wrong, because the rehearsal changes the very register those measurements depend on, so 27 leaves that genuinely move are held fixed and never appear as findings.
